title: Container Bookings: The Shipper's VGM Declaration Transmission
content:
For Container Bookings, the verified gross mass is declared by the shipper, who is the party responsible for it. The transmission of that declaration to the line is an action the customer performs through a tool of its own.

## What the transmission does

The shipper sends its own signed VGM declaration for a booking. A single transmission records the present moment as the time at which the line received the booking's VGM, and it replaces any receipt time recorded earlier on the booking. Nothing else on the booking changes and no charge is made. After the transmission the booking shows its VGM as received at that moment.

## Who runs it and how

The tool `submit_vgm_declaration_120f73ac` belongs to the customer. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over, and the customer themselves then run it, as the shipper transmitting its own declaration.

## Parameter

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `booking_id` | the reference number of the booking the declaration is for, as passed to the shipper by the service agent from the booking lookup | identifier |

## Receipt

The tool returns a text rendering of a dictionary confirming the transmission: `booking_id` (the booking on which the declaration was recorded), `document` (always `verified_gross_mass`) and `received_at` (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, in the local time of the clock the line records, being the moment recorded as receipt). A returned `received_at` means the declaration is on record.

## Contract Q&A

**Does the transmission itself book a fee?** No; it records the receipt time only.

**What if a receipt time was already on the booking?** The new transmission overwrites it with the current moment.
